absent: Remainder of put_prev_task_scx beyond the truncated prefix, including handling when previous retains slice and interacts with next task.
Complete signatures with return types for preempt reason mapping and scheduler dispatch helper where fragmentation omits the prefix.

Contracts and side effects of unrouted helpers for placement, eligibility, queue lookup, dequeue, enqueue, run queue switching, clock, runnable state, slice handling, tick control, class ordering, capability missing checks, migration state, container and shard resolution, balance callback queuing, operation state waiting, local dispatch, and event accounting.
Numeric values, widths and bit positions of ABI constants, flags, verdicts, reasons, capabilities and slice markers.
Exact blocking, interrupt and preemption rules for dispatch queue locks and run queue locks, including behavior when locks are contended or when dispatch drops the run queue lock.

Behavior on dispatch buffer overflow, on missing global queue or shard, on invalid destination identifiers, and on races with scheduler disable or CPU hotplug beyond the abort and online checks shown.
Configuration conditions selecting between alternate variants for scheduler membership, stay eligibility and empty capability sync.

findings.text: Interface attempts to transfer one eligible task from a named shared dispatch queue into the local queue of a given run queue and reports whether such a transfer occurred, retrying internally after certain remote races.
Interface selects the global dispatch queue associated with the node of a given run queue and delegates to the generic queue consumption routine with no additional enqueue modifiers.
Interface drains staged dispatch requests from the current CPU dispatch context in cursor order through per request finalization, then accounts the drained count and resets the cursor to empty.
Interface processes pending effective capability synchronizations for a run queue under its lock, exiting early when sub hierarchy support is absent or no request is queued.

Remote unlink records the current CPU as holder after detaching the task from its dispatch queue, releases the queue lock before exchanging run queue locks, then confirms holder stability and run queue identity with warnings on violation.
Remote consumption wrapper moves the task to the destination local queue on successful unlink and lock exchange, otherwise restores the original run queue lock and signals failure for caller retry.

Inter queue move forbids a local source, resolves a local destination run queue from its embedding, substitutes a global queue with fallback marking when remote execution is disallowed, then performs same CPU direct placement versus cross CPU remote placement versus shared to shared abbreviated removal plus enqueue, returning the destination run queue.

Consumption first tests queue list emptiness without locking as a fast miss path, then under lock iterates queued tasks, abandoning non bypass queues while aborting, handling same run queue tasks by direct local placement and remote tasks by eligibility check plus remote consumption with retry on failure.

Finalization claims tasks through operation states none, queueing, queued and dispatching, treating none and dispatching as already owned elsewhere, requiring sequence match and scheduler ownership for queued with event accounting on foreign ownership, attempting atomic transition to dispatching with retry, and waiting while queueing.

After a successful claim the finalizer resolves the destination queue from scheduler, run queue, requested identifier and task CPU, routing local destinations to a local helper and other destinations to a generic enqueue helper with slice and state clearing modifiers.
Scheduler membership test exists in two build variants, one comparing the RCU observed scheduler pointer against the expected scheduler and one unconditionally reporting membership.
Balance helper requires the run queue lock, does nothing unless a pending marker is set, otherwise queues the deferred balance work item and clears the marker.

Single dispatch selection synchronizes capabilities, emits a one time acquire notification after a prior release when the preempt feature is present, prefers a runnable previous task with remaining slice outside bypass, then existing local backlog, then scheduler dispatch, with a keep last fallback honoring enqueue last configuration and stay eligibility, plus a re enqueue scan when multiple local tasks include immediate ones.

Scheduler dispatch helper first tries the global queue, then honors bypass only or periodic bypass hosting behavior when bypass dispatch is enabled, gates on dispatch operation presence and online marking, then loops invoking the dispatch operation and flushing staged requests with rechecks for previous with slice plus local and global backlog, bounding iterations with a deferred kick, ending with a final bypass attempt.
Bypass dispatch activity is indicated by a nonzero enable depth counter read with an unlikely hint.

Effective capability synthesis scans all capability ordinals, tests mask membership for the given container identifier in the selected shard, and accumulates matching bits together with their implied companions.
Implication mapping grants enqueue and immediate enqueue for preempt, immediate enqueue for enqueue, and nothing for other inputs.

Capability synchronization drains queued requests privately, reinitializes list nodes, orders against enqueuers with a barrier, recomputes effective sets, tracks lost and gained bits, conditionally notifies schedulers with stashed previous context and flushes resulting dispatches, arms or clears idle renotify state on baseline gain or loss, and schedules a revocation scan when revoked bits intersect the re enqueue mask.
When the CPU is inactive the sync path discards queued requests by draining and reinitializing nodes without state changes, leaving re seeding to activation.
In builds without sub hierarchy support the capability synchronization routine is an empty inline performing no action.

Stay eligibility exists in two variants, one unconditionally true and one returning true without sub support or for migration disabled tasks, otherwise testing that no required base capability is missing for the task scheduler on that CPU.

Next task installation handles early core scheduling execution by dequeue notification plus dispatch removal when still queued, stamps execution start from the run queue clock, conditionally emits a running notification, clears runnable state, applies out of band slice updates, and maintains tick stop dependency and load averages based on infinite versus finite slice including full nohz handling.

Class switch notification acts only when the CPU preempt feature is enabled and the next class is at or above the extension class, invoking the release callback at most once until a later acquire clears the released marker.
Preempt reason mapping reports distinct codes for stop, deadline and realtime next classes and an unknown code for all others.

Previous task release starts with a release ordered kick counter increment, updates current accounting, ends an exhausted slice with a rescue continuation exception, conditionally emits a stopping notification, and re marks runnable state when still queued; content beyond the shown prefix is not visible in this lane.

Inter queue movement and consumption require both the dispatch queue lock and the source run queue lock on entry, assert both, release the dispatch queue lock before local placement or run queue lock exchange, and never hold two run queue locks at once.

Dispatch selection, scheduler dispatch looping and capability synchronization require the run queue lock held on entry, assert it, bracket scheduler callbacks with an in dispatch marker, and may temporarily drop and reacquire the run queue lock during callbacks and buffer flushing while privately held batch state remains valid.
Task extension state includes a holder CPU field, a scheduler association pointer, an atomic operation state with embedded sequence, flag bits including a queued marker, and a remaining slice value.
A dispatch queue carries a numeric identifier, a spin lock, and list linkage supporting unlocked emptiness testing and locked iteration.

Run queue extension state carries a local dispatch queue with task and immediate counts, a flag word, online plus in dispatch plus balance pending plus tick control plus renotify markers, a release marker, a kick counter, a deferred balance work item, a stashed dispatch previous pointer, and a lock free capability sync list.

Scheduler state carries an aborting marker, per CPU storage with dispatch context, per node global queues, an operation table with flags and dispatch plus acquire plus release plus running plus stopping plus capability updated handlers, a bypass depth counter, and per shard capability partitions.

Dispatch context carries a target run queue pointer plus staged count and cursor, while each staged entry carries a task reference, queue sequence, destination identifier, slice, virtual time and enqueue modifiers.
Per CPU scheduler state carries a capability sync list node, current and reported effective capability sets, and an idle renotify flag.
A capability shard holds per capability masks indexed by capability ordinal for container membership tests.
Consumption iteration can stall when a contended queue holds many affinitized tasks or when retries race bypass draining; exiting non bypass queues while aborting bounds the bypass transition case.

Repeated production of ineligible tasks can trap the dispatch loop with interrupts disabled; a bounded iteration count with deferred kicking forces a fresh scheduling cycle and allows watchdog progress.
Cross CPU unlink faces holder and run queue reassignment races; failure of holder stability or run queue identity validation causes consumption to fail and retry under correct locks.

Spurious dispatch, concurrent dequeue and re enqueue cycles can invalidate a staged claim; sequence mismatch, foreign ownership and failed atomic claiming all result in silent abandonment of that entry.
ABI identifiers for local and bypass dispatch queues distinguish per CPU local queues from bypass queues used during bypass operation.
ABI enqueue modifiers mark global fallback selection, slice application and operation state clearing during inter queue moves and finalization.
ABI operation state mask, state values and sequence mask encode none, queueing, queued and dispatching lifecycle with an embedded queue sequence number.
ABI run queue flag bits encode balance callback pending, in dispatch scope, online state, tick stop eligibility and sub hierarchy idle renotify.
ABI dispatch verdicts distinguish keep previous, local available and none outcomes, with a separate bound limiting dispatch loop iterations.
ABI scheduler operation flags control CPU preempt notifications and enqueue last handling, with event counters for foreign insertion, keep last retention and sub bypass dispatch.
ABI preempt reason codes identify stop, deadline, realtime and unknown preemptors, with a separate dequeue reason for core scheduling early execution.

ABI capability bits plus capability count plus re enqueue on loss mask plus revoke reason govern admission and revocation scanning, with an infinite slice marker and a tick dependency bit governing tick control.
ABI task flag for queued membership indicates scheduler owned queueing lifecycle and gates notifications plus local backlog and keep last decisions.
